text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank's Issue Department assets and liabilities rose by 78 milion marks by July 11, to 3.080 billion marks, central bank's figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet lifted a ban restricting repatriations of income generated by foreign investments of less than $50,000 in a move to boost foreign investments in the country, government officials said.
-- The Sofia municipality is expected to start talks on acquisition of a 25 percent stake in the Sofia's private television Nova Televisia, Sofia Municipal Council's chairman Antoan Nikolov said.
-- The Plovdiv City Court declared Bulgaria's private Agrobusinessbank insolvent on the basis of a claim filed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), court's chairman Krasimir Kolarov said.
The BNB took over Agrobusinessbank for one lev in 1995 in a move to protect depositors in the ailing bank.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet ratified a credit agreement with the World Bank to extend a $40 million 20-year loan with five years grace period for critical imports of grains, medicines and foods in Bulgaria, the government press office said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet suspended customs duties on imported grain harvesters until the end of the year in a bid to help collect this year's crop, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
-- Deputies from the Italian anti-mafia parliamentary commission arrived in Sofia to share experience with Bulgarian prosecution officials on organised crime prevention measures.
-- The European Investment Bank has expressed interest in funding 50 percent of the reconstructiion of the Sofia airport, deputy Prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- Bulgaria's Foreign ministry said it would coordinate European Union (EU) Phare programme's projects implemented in the country after the European Commission said it intended the Phare programme to act as financial instrument which would prepare EU associate members for full membership.
Phare programme's projects have been coordinated by the Trade ministry.

-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry is expected to tighten police control on the country's roads in a move to prevent strong arm criminal groups from buying wheat illegaly, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
